parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the conditions for a system to be in equilibrium.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Fig. 3.1 shows an airship in flight. The airship is propelled by identical fans that can be angled to control the motion of the airship.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

Fig. 3.1

The upthrust on the airship is $93\,000\text{ N}$.
The density of the surrounding air is $1.2\text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the volume of air displaced by the airship.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
When fully loaded, the weight of the airship is greater than the upthrust.
To maintain horizontal flight, the fans provide a total vertical force of $3.0 \times 10^3\text{ N}$ upwards on the airship.

Calculate the mass of the airship.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
At a certain time, the airship in (b) is stationary. The thrust force exerted by a fan on the airship is $2800\text{ N}$.

To produce this force, a mass of $64\text{ kg}$ of air is propelled through the blades of the fan in a time of $0.50\text{ s}$. Assume that this air is initially stationary at the entrance to the fan.

Calculate:

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: the change in momentum $\Delta p$ of the air propelled through the fan blades in this time

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: the speed of the air as it leaves the fan

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: the total kinetic energy of this air due to its movement through the fan.
